prompt: Create a landscape educational infographic with two main panels plus a bottom comparison strip. Keep the composition orthographic, tidy, and easy to read. Left panel: show a water chamber with the exact label 'Low Solute', a central semipermeable membrane, and a second chamber with the exact label 'High Solute'. Add a blue arrow crossing the membrane labeled exactly 'Natural Osmosis'. Right panel: show a high-pressure feed side with a pressure piston icon pushing inward, a membrane, a clean-water permeate side, a blue arrow crossing the membrane labeled exactly 'Reverse Osmosis', and retained contaminants staying on the feed side. Bottom strip: include a mini dead-end filtration sketch with water going straight into a filter, beside a cross-flow filtration sketch with feed water moving parallel to the membrane. Use only the requested labels.

Create a five-panel educational infographic about water quality metrics for reverse osmosis. Use a clean laboratory diagram style with strong separation between panels. Panel 1: a digital TDS meter immersed in a glass of water. Panel 2: a conductivity-to-TDS conversion chart featuring the exact text note '0.5 to 0.7'. Panel 3: an SDI test concept with a membrane disc becoming darker from fouling. Panel 4: LSI scaling risk shown as calcium scale depositing onto a membrane surface. Panel 5: chlorine symbols entering a carbon pre-filter block before a TFC membrane block, with a red warning icon near the membrane. Make the few required labels large and legible, and do not add extra text.

Create a landscape block diagram of a standard 5-stage domestic reverse osmosis system. Arrange the diagram clearly from left to right. Show the feed water inlet, sediment filter housing, carbon pre-filter housing, second carbon filter housing, and RO membrane housing. From the membrane block, show an upper branch with a permeate outlet, a check valve, a storage tank, and a faucet. Show a lower branch with a concentrate outlet, flow restrictor, and drain line. Add arrows and only these exact labels where appropriate: 'Feed', 'Permeate', and 'Concentrate'.

Create a comparison infographic with three vertical filter cutaways. Left: a melt-blown polypropylene sediment filter trapping dirt and silt. Middle: a granular activated carbon cartridge with irregular carbon granules adsorbing organics. Right: a carbon block cartridge with dense uniform media. Add a bottom strip with simple icons representing particle capture and chlorine removal. Include one highlighted note with the exact text 'Chloramines require Catalytic Carbon'. Keep the layout symmetrical and use no extra wording.

Create an exploded technical diagram of a spiral-wound reverse osmosis membrane. Show a permeate collection tube at the center. Around it, clearly separate and identify the layers visually: permeate carrier layer, polyamide thin-film active layer, polysulfone support layer, polyester backing, and feed spacer mesh. Add arrows showing feed water entering, purified permeate moving inward, and concentrate moving outward. Include a small inset explaining concentration polarization, with a salt boundary layer building up and cross-flow turbulence disrupting it. Keep the overall image clean, textbook-like, and uncluttered.

Create a left-to-right process diagram for post-filtration and remineralization after reverse osmosis. Block 1: RO permeate with the exact label 'Low pH'. Block 2: a carbon polishing filter. Block 3: a remineralization cartridge containing media. Block 4: a glass of finished water with the exact label 'Balanced pH'. Add small chemistry icons suggesting carbon dioxide absorption and buffering restoration. Use only the requested text.

Create a three-stage cutaway educational diagram of a hydropneumatic reverse osmosis storage tank. Show three tanks side by side as a progression. Left tank: nearly empty, with a small water volume, large air chamber, and the exact label '7 to 8 PSI'. Middle tank: partially filled, with a compressed air chamber and rising pressure arrows. Right tank: nearly full, with a highly compressed air chamber and a note reading exactly 'ASV Closes at 2/3 Line Pressure'. Also include the exact text 'Boyle's Law: P1V1 = P2V2'. Make the progression visually obvious and keep the typography readable.

Create a split comparison infographic of reverse osmosis pump options. Left side: feed water enters an electric booster pump, then a pressure switch, then a membrane housing. Include the exact labels '80 to 100 PSI' and 'Electric Booster'. Right side: show a brine line driving a hydro-mechanical permeate pump, and a permeate line being pushed into the tank. Include the exact label 'Permeate Pump (ERP)'. Use colored arrows to distinguish water and energy flow, and keep the two halves balanced.

Create an educational infographic about reverse osmosis waste water and efficiency. Top section: feed water splits into a smaller permeate stream and a larger concentrate stream, with the exact text 'Recovery Ratio: 1 to 4'. Bottom section: three comparison blocks showing a correctly sized flow restrictor, a restrictor that is too small and causes fouling, and a restrictor that is too large and causes excess drain flow. Keep the cause-and-effect differences easy to compare at a glance.

Create a three-column comparison visual for choosing a reverse osmosis system. Column 1: a standard under-sink tanked system with filter housings, membrane, and tank. Column 2: a compact tankless direct-flow unit with an integrated booster pump. Column 3: simplified icons for countertop and whole-house options. Under each column, show compact badges for output, noise, and electricity. Add one highlighted warning note for tankless systems with the exact text 'Warning: TDS Creep'. Use a clean shopping-guide style without extra copy.

Create a workshop flat-lay illustration organized into three clearly separated groups. Group 1 must be labeled exactly 'Included with system' and show three cylindrical filter housings, three filter cartridges, a housing wrench, a membrane housing, a small post-filter assembly, a round pressurized storage tank, coiled connection tubing, and a small faucet. Group 2 must be labeled exactly 'Essential tools' and show a powerful drill with a 12 mm pyramidal steel bit and a stone drill bit, adjustable wrenches, PTFE tape, a digital TDS pen meter, a sharp knife, and two types of screws. Group 3 must be labeled exactly 'Optional' and show a pressure gauge with a flexible hose, needle-nose pliers, a tubular wrench with a bar, a dual-size housing spanner, and a small tube of food-grade silicone lubricant. Do not add any other text labels.

Create an under-sink plumbing teaching diagram for installing a domestic reverse osmosis system. Top left: cold-water angle stop. Center: mounted pre-filters and membrane. Bottom center: storage tank. Top right: faucet on the sink deck. Bottom right: drain saddle mounted above the P-trap on the vertical tailpiece. Use different line colors for feed, permeate, brine, and drain tubing, and keep the routing easy to follow.

Create a four-step startup sequence graphic for a new reverse osmosis system. Block 1: new filters and a dry membrane. Block 2: system filling the storage tank with the exact label '2 to 3 hours'. Block 3: faucet opened and dark first water being discarded. Block 4: a repeat-cycle icon. Add one warning callout with the exact text 'Do Not Consume First Tank'. Arrange the steps in a clear left-to-right sequence.

Create a safety-focused diagram for reverse osmosis leak testing. Main block: a complete RO system under static pressure with the most common leak points highlighted at housings and tubing connections. Side block 1: a close-up of a push fitting with a blue collet clip correctly installed. Side block 2: a cabinet-floor leak detector shutoff valve using an expanding sponge mechanism. Keep the image instructional and uncluttered.

Create an instructional figure about handling an RO membrane correctly. Left: a membrane cartridge with the brine seal highlighted. Middle: a membrane housing with a clear insertion-direction arrow. Right: a close-up of permeate tube O-rings with silicone grease being applied. Add a red warning symbol over a jar with the exact text 'No Petroleum Jelly'. Favor clean close-up teaching visuals over decorative elements.

Create a monitoring diagram for inline TDS measurement in an RO system. Show a feed water line with an inline TDS probe, an RO membrane housing, a permeate line with a second inline TDS probe, and a digital monitor. The monitor must show the exact labels 'Feed TDS', 'Permeate TDS', and 'Rejection %'. Add a small inset showing a thermistor for temperature compensation. Keep the signal flow obvious.

Create a maintenance dashboard infographic for reverse osmosis service intervals. Main section: calendar-style bars for sediment filter, carbon filters, and membrane replacement intervals. Side inset 1: delta-pressure monitoring with a pressure gauge before and after the pre-filters. Side inset 2: biological loading shown as bacteria risk in an old carbon filter. Keep the dashboard clean and readable with visual hierarchy.

Create a symptom-to-cause diagnostic flowchart for reverse osmosis faults. Top row: three symptom boxes labeled exactly 'Continuous Drain', 'Rapid Cycling', and 'Low Flow'. Branches should lead downward to simple icon-based root causes including a failed check valve, a waterlogged tank, and membrane fouling. Use a crisp flowchart structure and only the requested text.

Create a stepwise sanitization protocol diagram for a reverse osmosis system. Show the sequence: remove all filters, add bleach to the first housing, run the system until disinfectant reaches the faucet, let it sit pressurized for contact time, then flush thoroughly. Include one caution panel with the exact text 'Flush Completely Before Use'. Present the steps in a clear procedural order.

Create a hardware architecture block diagram for an IoT-enabled reverse osmosis monitor. Show a feed-line sensor, permeate-line sensor, flow sensor, central ESP32 microcontroller board, Wi-Fi transmission waves, and a smartphone dashboard panel. Use signal arrows connecting sensors to the microcontroller and then to the phone. Keep the layout neat and engineering-oriented.

Create a two-part comparison infographic for advanced reverse osmosis upgrades. Left: a UV-C sterilizer as the final stage, showing the glowing blue lamp, quartz sleeve, and water path. Right: an auto-flush solenoid valve on the brine line bypassing the restrictor, with a strong flush arrow sweeping across the membrane surface. Make the two upgrades visually distinct and easy to compare.

Create a large-scale whole-house reverse osmosis system block diagram. Show raw water feed, pretreatment skid, high-pressure pump, parallel industrial membrane vessels, a large atmospheric storage tank, a repressurization delivery pump, and household plumbing distribution. Add one warning callout with the exact text 'Use PEX or CPVC Only'. Keep the system architecture readable despite the larger scale.

Create a reuse-pathways diagram for reverse osmosis concentrate. Place the RO system at the center with a brine output line. Branch the brine output to three destinations: a hot-water line via a zero-waste pump, a toilet cistern refill, and a landscape-irrigation rain barrel. Add one side note with the exact text 'Keep Away From Sunlight'. Keep the branching paths clean and visually balanced.

Create a service-business model diagram for residential reverse osmosis maintenance. Show multiple installed customer RO units transmitting wireless telemetry, a central monitoring dashboard on a computer, a technician driving a van dispatched from alerts, and a recurring monthly subscription icon. Present the flow from installed devices to remote monitoring to service action clearly.

Create a final recap course-map infographic with five large connected blocks arranged from left to right. The blocks must contain exactly these labels: 'Foundations', 'System Design', 'Installation', 'Maintenance', and 'Advanced'. Connect the blocks with thick clean progression arrows. Keep the composition bold, simple, and highly legible.
